videos.script: A table orders three coffees and two slices of cake, and pays with a loyalty card on its ninth stamp. How much do they pay? {{order}} Ask a model for the amount alone, and it may answer sixty-six. That is the price with every coffee paid for. {{direct}} Ask it to work the order out step by step, and it writes the steps first. The card reaches ten stamps. One coffee is free. Then the total, fifty-four. {{steps}} Nothing about the model changed. What changed is the text in front of the answer. {{text}} A model writes one token at a time, and each step it writes becomes part of what the next token is predicted from. {{tokens}} In this lesson you ask for that chain of steps, read the answer out of it reliably, and count what the extra words cost. {{cost}} You also see a chain that reads perfectly and is wrong. {{wrong}}
